note.question: When should firms replace proprietary loyalty programs with a coalition, and how should the coalition set price, reward, and membership size to discriminate among customers?
note.overview: A coalition anticipates forward-looking customers' dynamic purchase and reward-redemption decisions when choosing price, reward, and coalition size. The equilibrium design problem compares coalition and proprietary loyalty programs through the induced strategic customer response.

coverage.note: The existing independently audited model map was decomposed into Mini-style components and linked back to the page-preserving source extraction.

models.name: Infinite-horizon reward design with heterogeneous valuation and shopping intensity
models.summary: A coalition anticipates forward-looking customers' dynamic purchase and reward-redemption decisions when choosing price, reward, and coalition size. The equilibrium design problem compares coalition and proprietary loyalty programs through the induced strategic customer response.
objects: A coalition program designer acting for participating firms
inputs: The program designer knows the population shares of four valuation-shopping-intensity segments
A customer knows her valuation, shopping intensity, current reward state, price, reward, expiration rate, and coalition size
Customer arrivals and reward expiration are stochastic, but their rates are common knowledge
The base coalition is symmetric and abstracts from direct competition among participating firms
decisions: The coalition chooses price and reward for a fixed membership size
Each arriving customer chooses whether to purchase
The analysis compares the optimized coalition outcome with proprietary and no-reward program benchmarks
assumptions: There are n symmetric independent firms, zero marginal cost, a unit customer mass, and an infinite continuous-time horizon
Customer visits to each firm are independent Poisson processes with exogenous shopping intensities
Customers have one of two valuations and one of two shopping intensities, with arbitrary correlation across the two dimensions
A purchase earns one cash-like reward redeemable at any coalition firm; the reward does not accumulate and expires at an exponential rate
Price is constant, reward does not exceed price, and customers discount future surplus in the base model

models.method: The authors solve a two-state continuous-time customer dynamic program, derive purchase thresholds and optimal price-reward design for fixed coalition size, optimize membership size, compare coalition, proprietary, and no-program profits, and study extensions with no discounting, point accumulation, asymmetric firms, and altered reward renewal.
